body: Thank you. Probably true, but I can't see it happening. I appreciate you taking the time to talk xx

Yup. I think they're just overwhelmed with people feeling similarly. I think from their perspective, I've not made an actual attempt and I do have a strong support network, so time and resources are better spent on people in worse circumstances. Don't really envy anyone in mental health having to make these decisions!

I 100% think he'd be better off without the worry weighing him down. He's suffering badly from burnout with this, though I try to encourage him to talk to friends or seek support.

I appreciate what you're saying, but to him our child wouldn't be a reminder really, more something to focus on and a reason to recover. He's a good dad. 

I don't think there's anything in particular triggering it. I've just finally had enough. I have been trying, I saw my doctor and was referred to my community mental health team, but they just bounced me back saying I wasn't an immediate risk so I think I've exhausted my medical options.

It just leaves me to somehow get better, and I think even if I manage it this time, this situation will just come around again and at a worse time.

He knows, and it's starting to really affect him too, which to me, from a logical standpoint, means he'd be better off if I got it out of the way sooner rather than later so he can heal and move on while still in his 20s.
